title: Race condition in dining module message updates

evidence.quote: setMsgs(prev => [...prev.filter(m => m._id !== ts), { role: 'assistant', content: reply }])

reasoning: If the user sends multiple messages rapidly (or double-clicks the send button despite disabled state), multiple askRex calls can execute concurrently. Each generates a unique ts (Date.now()), but the loading state is shared. The final setMsgs call filters by _id: ts, which works per-request, but React state batching and async timing could cause messages to arrive out of order or duplicate loading messages to appear briefly. The disabled={loading} guard is present but doesn't prevent race if user clicks before loading is set.
reproduction: Remove or bypass the disabled={loading} check. Rapidly click send twice. Two concurrent askRex calls execute. Both add loading messages with different _id values. Responses may arrive out of order, causing the UI to show stale loading indicators or messages in wrong sequence.
recommendation: Use a ref-based request ID or cancel token to ensure only one request is in flight. Cancel previous requests when a new one starts (AbortController). Ensure loading state prevents duplicate submissions before state updates propagate.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No concurrency tests exist. The disabled guard is present but not tested under rapid interaction scenarios.
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: simulate rapid askRex calls and verify only one request completes. Integration test: confirm UI does not allow duplicate submissions even under slow state updates.
minimumFixScope: src/src/portal/modules/dining.tsx askRex function: add AbortController to cancel previous requests or use a ref to track in-flight request ID
